remainingTradesContextAlignment.review: Re-read the complete unmodified OS mosaic. The southern Marshgate arm previously ran through Crown/Johnson instead of the public street east of its walls. aldersonRopeAlignment.review: Raw OS five-foot map re-read along the lane between the eastern rope-works wall and the eastern street edge. Preserve northern-arm controls0–8, then fit the south bend clear of the mapped drying house and follow the eastern rope frontage to the lane head at the railway underpass boundary. The former tail cut through the mapped eastern rope roof and extended into the railway. Existing interpreted 7 m carriageway and normal 1.1 m shoulder retained; no new road connection or bridge inferred.

notes: High Street bridge names follow the 19th-century transposition: Pegshole over Three Mills Back River; St Thomas over western Waterworks arm; St Michael over eastern arm.
Bow Bridge: one granite-faced span completed 1839. c1900 appearance retained; 1901–06 construction stages unresolved.
User-supplied 1851 guide illustration and Mackenzie painting show the earlier multi-arch bridge, retained as historical comparison only.
St Thomas brick arch count is not established by the written source; one opening is a modelling estimate.
Surface materials, widths and heights are estimates. No 1933 Groves Bridge or modern flyover.

Three provisional lane connections cover small discrepancies between road tracing and independently registered GIS banks at Marshgate Lane, Cook’s Road and the Three Mills yard. Their deck/culvert structure is unresolved, unlike the five documented High Street bridges.
